notes: Route: the site's own reverse-chronological listing https://www.lavoz.com.ar/lo-ultimo/N/ (canonical /ultimas-noticias/), N = 1,2,3... Each page is server-rendered Next.js and carries <script id="__NEXT_DATA__"> whose pageProps.matchConfig.content holds 20 story objects with the fields url and publishedDate (site-stated publication time, offset -03:00); I take the local date, i.e. the first 10 characters. Fetches: /lo-ultimo/ HTTP 200, pages up to N=300 HTTP 200 returning older pages monotonically (N=50 -> 2026-10-20, N=150 -> 2026-10-09, N=300 -> 2026-09-23/24), so 290 pages cover the whole 2026-09-25..2026-10-25 window; walked 290 pages, read 5,545 in-window URLs (107-261 per day) in 9m37s at polite_fetch's 2 req/s cap for this host. robots.txt (HTTP 200) allows / for User-agent: * and only disallows /_next/, /pf/resource/, a few test paths and AI crawlers named by name, so /lo-ultimo/ is permitted. Dead ends, all tried: the Arc XP endpoints advertised in robots.txt (/arc/outboundfeeds/sitemap.xml?outputType=xml, .../feeds/sitemap/, .../news-sitemap/, .../v3/all/stories/) all return HTTP 530 with an empty body, as does /rss/portada.xml, so no sitemap or JSON content API is reachable; /sitemap.xml, /sitemap_index.xml, /news-sitemap.xml, /archivo/2026/10/20/, /2026/10/20/ and /cordoba/?page=2 all return 404; /cordoba/ itself is 404 (sections are e.g. /sucesos/, /politica/); /rss/ is a catch-all that re-serves the homepage, but /rss/lo-ultimo/ does work (HTTP 200, 20 items) - it only carries the newest 20 stories and its lastBuildDate was stale, so it cannot cover a month and was not used. Verified: 4 re-fetched articles from 2026-09-28, 10-05, 10-14, 10-22 each returned HTTP 200, 5,487-8,114 characters of body text, and a JSON-LD datePublished equal to the listed date (same day, e.g. 2026-10-14T22:00:10Z for a listed 2026-10-14). TSV: 5,545 rows, 5,545 unique URLs, no header, every date inside the window. Note on completeness: /lo-ultimo/ is the site's whole 'ultimas noticias' stream (about 180 stories a day) but there is no way to prove it holds every section's output; section-by-section listing pages were 404, so this route cannot be cross-checked against a second source.
